title: stacker deploy --target server writes every project to the same remote path, causing real cross-project deployment damage
excerpt:
produced via `stacker-projects/duplicati` colliding with a pre-existing `stacker-projects/rallly` deployment, both targeting the same `EXISTING_SERVER_HOST`, in trydirect/stacker-project-examples
- Related: #235 (same bug class, `--target local` variant)
---
Updating with a more severe detail found on further investigation: this wasn't just compose-file thrashing — **rallly's actual database volume was recreated empty**, i.e. real data loss.

\`docker volume inspect project_rallly_db\` shows \`CreatedAt: 2026-08-20T17:40:21Z\` — today, during this exact testing window — and \`du -sh\` on it shows only 8.0K (empty, no real data). Postgres now refuses to start: \`Database is uninitialized and superuser password is not specified\` (rallly's own compose has \`POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ''\`, which was presumably fine against the *original* initialized volume but fails cold-start validation against a fresh empty one).

So the actual sequence was worse than "wrote a different compose file over the old one": something in the \`--target server\` deploy path for \`duplicati\` appears to have torn down and recreated volumes under the shared \`project\` compose project scope too — not just the compose file/containers. This raises the severity from "silent overwrite" to "silent data loss" for whatever was in the previous occupant's volumes.

**Problem:** VS Code fails to open the project in a Dev Container when using [Colima](https://github.com/abacusai/colima) instead of Docker Desktop. The `docker pull` command fails with:

excerpt:
Found by the first live run, in the pipeline P-03 reads as its verdict.

`tests/adapters/execution/test_container.py::test_a_job_that_exceeds_its_memory_limit_is_killed_and_says_so` passed in CI at 12:35 and failed at 12:44 on the same runner image, with essentially the same tree, and passes locally on macOS with Docker 29.1.2. It is flaky.

```

E  AssertionError: JobExit(code=137, killed=None, reason='the unit exited with 137')

**Why.** The container adapter reads `state["OOMKilled"]` from the engine's inspect and maps it to `killed="memory"` (`src/taktus/adapters/driven/execution/container/adapter.py`). With `runtime.type = "docker"` and `docker.network_mode = "bridge"`, concurrent sandbox creation

title: Root-stage mkdirs under $HOME break the user-stage volume mkdirs
excerpt:
A template that creates a directory under `$HOME` in its `root.Dockerfile` leaves it owned by `root`. The generated user stage later runs `mkdir -p` for every declared volume path as `${USER}`, so any volume nested under that directory fails the build.

The `jupyter` template hits this: its `root.Dockerfile` runs `mkdir -p $HOME/.local`, so a volume at `.local/share/<name>` cannot be created.

Reproduce with:

```json
[
  {
    "name": "jupyter_repro",
    "templates": ["jupyter"],
    "volumes": { "state": ".local/share/example" }
  }
]
```

`docker compose build jupyter_repro` fails with:

```
mkdir: cannot create directory '/home/user/.local/share': Permission denied
```

The generated Dockerfile shows the cause — `USER root` creates `$HOME/.local`, then the volume mkdirs run after `USER ${USER}`:

```
USER root
# --- jupyter ---
RUN mkdir -p $HOME/.local && \
    mkdir -p $HOME/.jupyter

USER ${USER}
RUN mkdir -p \
    $HOME/.local/share/example
```

Possible fixes: `chown` root-stage `$HOME` directories back to the container user, emit the volume mkdirs before the root fragments, or drop the redundant `mkdir` calls from `jupyter/root.Dockerfile` since the volume mkdirs already cover them.
